context: Dual-axis time series showing 18 months of daily temperature (line, left axis) and weekly rainfall (bars, right axis) with explicit gap handling: dashed bridges and labeled gap regions for temperature sensor outages, hatched bars for missing rainfall periods, and shaded reference bands for normal ranges.
first_impression: Busy but well-managed — the seasonal temperature arc reads immediately, gaps are unambiguous, and the color-coded dual axes largely defuse the usual dual-axis confusion.
what_works: Color-coding the axes and series to the same hues (blue=temp, cyan=rain) significantly reduces the dual-axis cognitive tax; gap handling is exemplary with four reinforcing signals — shaded region, dashed bridge, boundary circles, and text labels — so missing data is impossible to overlook. The 3-hue palette stays well within color overload limits.
what_doesnt: The dense daily temperature line layered over semi-transparent cyan bars creates visual competition in the mid-chart region where both series overlap near the 10–25°C normal band, making it harder to read individual rainfall bar heights; the dual-axis caution footnote is rendered at 10px in light grey and will be missed by most viewers despite carrying a genuine interpretive warning.
